name: KING OYSTER
blurb: A CRAFT CROP. COLD, BRIGHT, CYCLIC CO2.

overview.v: A craft crop, not a meal ticket. Not worth growing without cooling and air handling.
Sells like hotcakes. A single steak-like mushroom is less intimidating than clusters.
Mediterranean and North African varieties on carrot-family plants. Weakly parasitic.

cultivation.v: Soy-based Master's Mix made consistent fruiting possible.
Industry standard, no number given. Low rates lengthen colonisation and cut yield sharply.
Use just-colonized spawn. 0.5-1 week extra makes a brick with some stroma.

timeline.v: 14-18 days. Some 10. Up to 3 weeks if spawn is poorly spread.
Move to fruit as soon as colonized. Left too long they skin over.

climate.v: 10-16 °C (50-60 °F) ideal. Trouble above 16 °C. No reliable pinning above about 17 °C. The 16 °C room is at the edge.
Ryan grows kings at about 65 °F (18 °C) with extra AC.
Fairly high and steady. Constant fresh-air exchange leaves RH flat at 80-85%, which is not wanted. No target number.
Cyclic control from a CO2 controller, not a constant fan. High CO2 gives pale, flat caps.
Bright, even and intense. Strongly light-triggered; fruits from the top centre.

yield_.v: About 2-2.25 lb (0.9-1.0 kg), not the 4 lb of other oysters.
About 0.86 lb/block aggregate (0.6-0.75 by lot match). Far under Cap n Stem's figure.

hazards.v: Watch cap tops and streaking stems. Stays where water sits on stripped blocks.
Early failures: 250 CFM fans running constantly, no CO2 meter.
Appear in very high humidity. Different from rose comb.

notes.v: Fruit cold, bright and evenly lit, with cyclic CO2 control.
